diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, when $\tau=2/(L+\mu)$, we have the well-known best local linear convergence rate for $\big\{\phi^n\big\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$

issues.failure_explanation: The analysis optimizes one constant step for a fixed preconditioner, not all Riemannian gradient methods allowed by the variable-step formulation. Indeed, put c=(L+mu)/2 and h=(L-mu)/2. Alternating steps 1/(c±h/sqrt(2)) gives a linearized two-step polynomial bounded on [mu,L] by h²/(2c²-h²), whose per-step factor is strictly smaller than h/c. When mu is sufficiently close to L, both steps are within the stable-step interval. Thus the constant-step factor is not a universal lower limit on gradient-method rates.

failure_location.quote: which is the best rate one can possibly get for a Riemannian gradient method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the optimality claim to the minimax choice of one constant step for a fixed preconditioner and its spectral interval; remove optimality claims over variable-step methods or all metrics.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimality over Riemannian gradient methods and preconditioners exceeds the fixed-metric, constant-step result actually established.
issues.title: Constant-step optimization is overstated as universal optimality
issues.why_classification: A substantive optimality promise must be narrowed, but the comparable constant-step convergence result can remain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall that $E''(\phi_g)$ is an unbounded, self-adjoint, coercive operator with compact resolvent.

issues.failure_explanation: The established necessary condition concerns the tangent space, whereas the proof invokes convexity and coercivity of the quadratic form on the entire ambient space. Assumption (A3) does not require f' to be nonnegative, so full-space positivity of E'' is not established. The preceding Gårding inequality is not full-space coercivity. Consequently, the stated justification for weak lower semicontinuity and attainment is unsupported. The final spectral appendix repeats the same unsupported coercivity assertion.

failure_location.quote: Since the bilinear form $a(\cdot,\cdot)$ is symmetric and coercive, $F$ is convex and coercive, and is defined on $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply weak lower semicontinuity to the continuous quadratic form restricted to the closed space N_phi M, where the necessary condition supplies positivity. For the final computation of L, use the already available compactness argument in G-spectrum instead of unsupported ambient coercivity.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of attainment, the positive normal spectral gap, and the subsequent positive-mu convergence arguments have a local proof gap.
issues.title: The spectral-gap proof assumes unsupported full-space convexity
issues.why_classification: The existing necessary condition, continuity, and Gårding estimate provide a short local bypass without changing the spectral-gap conclusion or rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we utilize respectively the standard   eighth-order and second-order central finite  difference method to discretize

issues.failure_explanation: Morse–Bott requires an exact continuum kernel and a positive gap beyond the symmetry directions. The evidence consists of approximate eigenvalues of a finite-difference problem, printed to eight decimal places. No eigenvalue enclosures or discretization-error bounds transfer their apparent equality and separation to the continuum Hessian. In particular, equality after rounding cannot establish exact multiplicity two.

failure_location.quote: In particular, for the numerical example to be provided later, we have verified that the Gross-Pitaevskii energy functional  indeed qualifies as a Morse-Bott functional.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the experiment as numerical evidence consistent with Morse–Bott. Retaining an exact verification claim requires certified spectral bounds and a continuum-discretization comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The example supplies numerical evidence, not verification that the hypotheses of the conditional local-convergence theorems hold for the continuum problem.
issues.title: Rounded discrete eigenvalues do not verify the continuum Morse–Bott property
issues.why_classification: Weakening verification to empirical support is a limited substantive loss; the conditional analytical results need not change.

issues.failure_explanation: The admissible choice f(s)=s^(3/2) satisfies (A3) with theta=2, but F(s)=2s^(5/2)/5. Its normalized line-search energy generally contains noninteger powers of |phi+tau d|² and of 1+tau²||d||², rather than a rational function of tau. The asserted rationale for general exact-line-search efficiency therefore fails outside the polynomial special case.

issues.title: The line-search energy need not be rational
issues.why_classification: The line-search scope must be narrowed, although the underlying gradient framework and convergence analysis can remain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: defined for each $\phi \in H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ as a symmetric and coercive real linear operator from $H_0^1(\mathcal{D})$ to $H^{-1}(\mathcal{D})$

issues.failure_explanation: For P=I, the induced quadratic form is the L² norm, which is not coercive or complete in the stated H¹ setting. Moreover, for a general H¹ iterate, H_phi phi is only in H^(-1); the inverse of the canonical L² identification cannot turn it into an H¹ tangent vector. Thus this purported instance of the update is not generally defined on the paper's state space, even though the remark correctly distinguishes the latter four preconditioners as satisfying (A6).

failure_location.quote: All these methods can be encompassed within the framework of \eqref{Riem-Opt-menthod}, with the respective preconditioners being \(\mathcal{P}_{\phi} = \mathcal{I},\ a\mathcal{I} - \frac{1}{2}\Delta\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Limit the continuous H¹ framework to coercive Sobolev metrics, and identify the L² method only after spatial discretization or under a separately specified regularity/domain formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed inclusion of the continuous L²-projected method is not valid at the stated regularity.
issues.title: The L² preconditioner is not an admissible continuous H¹ instance
issues.why_classification: A claimed method class must be excluded from the continuous framework or given a separate construction; the coercive Sobolev cases survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists $\theta\in\left[0,3\right)$ such that $f'(s^2)s^2$ is Lipschitz continuous

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted L² product bounds do not follow from H¹ regularity in dimension three. For example, f(s)=s^(3/2), theta=2, is admissible. Taking real phi=v equal near the origin to a cutoff times |x|^(-2/5) gives H¹ functions, but the product f'(rho_phi)|phi|²v is proportional to |phi|³v and is not in L². The final L^p bounds are instead compatible with an H^(-1) estimate using an H¹ test function.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the L² product estimates by H^(-1) dual estimates and apply Hölder with the test function in L⁶. This gives the stated p0 and preserves the intended final bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The compact-type and local-Lipschitz estimates used later have an invalid intermediate estimate for permitted nonlinearities.
issues.title: Nonlinear products are incorrectly estimated in L²
issues.why_classification: A short duality estimate repairs the proof without changing assumptions, conclusions, or convergence rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Descent only controls the weighted sum of C_tau_n times the squared gradient. No nonvanishing or nonsummability condition on these coefficients is imposed. Starting at a noncritical point, one can choose positive summable steps with sufficiently small total length so that all iterates remain in a neighborhood where the gradient stays nonzero; the sequence then converges to a noncritical point. The same missing uniform control also prevents the unrestricted energy-drop equivalence in E-eq-Phi: as steps tend to zero, a one-step energy drop can be arbitrarily smaller than the remaining energy gap.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require steps in a compact subinterval of the relevant admissible interval, giving a uniform positive descent coefficient. A nonsummability condition can suffice for subsequential stationarity alone, but not for the stated uniform energy-drop equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: Part (ii) of the global theorem and the unrestricted uniform comparison with one-step energy drops are false as stated; energy monotonicity alone survives.
issues.title: Arbitrarily small steps do not guarantee stationarity

issues.failure_explanation: Property-P(iii) is stated only for points in an H¹ neighborhood. A bounded weakly convergent subsequence need not eventually enter such a neighborhood, and local H¹ Lipschitz continuity does not imply weak sequential continuity. The proof therefore invokes the proposition outside its stated hypotheses before strong convergence has been established.

issues.failure_explanation: H¹-Lipschitz dependence does not imply the stronger L^p-Lipschitz assertions in Property-P(iii), including the multiplier and gradient-minus-identity estimates. For example, adding a nonnegative bounded smooth coefficient a(||phi||_H¹²) times I to H0 preserves symmetry, coercivity, and the lower-order structure, but the coefficient can change along small, bounded high-frequency perturbations whose L^p norms tend to zero. At nearby noncritical points this can change the compact part of the gradient. Morse–Bott at the minimizer does not remove that dependence.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, it is not necessarily coercive even at $\phi_g$.

issues.failure_explanation: Morse–Bott gives positivity of K=E''(phi_g)-lambda_g I on the normal tangent space, not on the full ambient space required by the preconditioner definition. A small positive mass shift cannot remove an arbitrary negative ambient eigenvalue. In particular, <K phi_g,phi_g>=2 integral f'(rho_g)rho_g², whose sign is not controlled by (A3). The proposed operator can therefore be indefinite or singular, so its inverse and induced Hilbert norm cannot be assumed admissible. The final appendix's ordering of the full-space Hessian spectrum has the same missing ambient-positivity premise.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that the linear operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $X$ satisfies the condition $\rho(T)=\rho<1$

issues.failure_explanation: For every fixed positive epsilon, choosing tau smaller than both 1/L and epsilon/mu gives max{|1-tau mu|,|1-tau L|}+epsilon=1-tau mu+epsilon>1. Thus the displayed factor is not a linear-convergence rate throughout the quantified interval. The stability lemma permits epsilon sufficiently small for a fixed operator, not one fixed positive epsilon uniformly down to tau=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix tau in (0,2/L) first, then choose epsilon smaller than both 1-max{|1-tau mu|,|1-tau L|} and 2/tau-L, with the neighborhood and constants chosen accordingly.

issues.title: The claimed rate factor need not be a contraction over the stated step interval
issues.why_classification: This standard local parameter condition preserves coverage of every stable fixed step and the same meaningful rate formula.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited upper bound is defined on the L²-orthogonal normal space N, whereas the proof only projects d_n into the full tangent space. A general admissible metric can couple symmetry and normal directions. On one such block, take K=diag(0,1) and P=[[1,b],[b,1]], |b|<1. The quotient on N=span(e2) is 1, but on the P-horizontal vector (-b,1) it is 1/(1-b²). Thus the claimed L need not bound the gradient direction. Adding an uncoupled normal mode shows that the true condition number can be arbitrarily worse; for b²>1/2, the advertised step tau=1 can even be linearly unstable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L in the generic local descent and convergence results by the supremum of K/P on the full tangent space. Alternatively, redo the spectral and alignment analysis on the P-orthogonal complement of the symmetry directions, or impose an explicit block-orthogonality condition.
issues.overall_effect: The generic-preconditioner local descent constant, step interval, and quantitative convergence rate are unsupported. The special shifted-Hessian metric avoids this particular symmetry-normal coupling, so its result is not a dependent of this root.
issues.title: The normal-space spectral bound is incorrectly applied to tangent directions
issues.why_classification: The supported unrestricted repair can shrink the permitted steps and worsen the promised condition-number rate by an arbitrarily large amount; preserving the original constants instead excludes metrics currently admitted by (A6).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The first two eigenfunctions are given by $v_1 = i\phi_g$ and $v_2 = i\mathcal{L}_z \phi_g / \|i\mathcal{L}_z \phi_g\|_{L^2}$

issues.failure_explanation: For the prescribed vectors, (v1,v2)_L² equals (phi_g,L_z phi_g)_L² divided by ||L_z phi_g||_L². None of the assumptions makes this angular-momentum expectation zero. Linear independence of phase and rotation generators does not imply their orthogonality, and self-adjointness does not force orthogonality within a repeated eigenspace.
